mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate margins and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
regime_hint: high inflation and high rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average by more than 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when HOUST exceeds its 6-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a labor market expansion with low unemployment, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) growth and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon, such that quarters with above-median GDPC1 growth see positive 5-day returns on average.
failure_condition: The correlation between quarterly GDPC1 growth and average 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
